summary: 4 spend denials this session, all read-only false positives, and the agent has no way to disposition them: ADR-0016 refuses both grant and dismiss to the agent, and dismiss is the verb that records a false positive. The backstop will therefore fire on every Stop for the rest of this session.
tried: Diagnosed the root cause by reading scripts/spend/guard.py rather than executing anything: _segments() at line 208 splits on the pipe character BEFORE quotes are stripped, so a quoted alternation is torn into fragments with unbalanced quotes and text inside quotes reaches COMMITTING as if it were a command. Verified against a live denial. Wrote it up in docs/observatory.md and as queue item 5 in the handoff. Did NOT fix the guard: highest-stakes control in the repo, three other guards broke today by being fixed, and a false positive on a read-only command fails in the safe direction.

Could not record the disposition: tessera-authorize dismiss is on the guard's own SELF_AUTHORIZING deny list, so the agent-facing path for 'this was a false positive' does not exist. Saying so in prose satisfies the hook's text but leaves no machine-readable trace, so the backstop re-fires.
options: Fix the tokenisation: strip quoted spans before _segments() splits. Must not blind the guard to a wrapper-led command that legitimately quotes a boot verb, which is what WRAPPER exists to catch.
Allow the agent 'dismiss' but not 'grant' — dismiss writes an event and never an envelope, so it commits nothing; ADR-0016's argument was about self-authorization, which dismiss is not.
Leave both as-is and accept that agent-encountered false positives are recorded only in prose — cheapest, and defensible if false positives stay rare.
status: resolved:moot — ADR-0029 retired the in-band spend guard; all three options concerned a mechanism that no longer exists
